name: Old Farm District
label: Old Farm District
about_prose: Old Farm District sits in Bend's southeast quadrant, roughly bounded by Highway 97 on the west, SE 27th Street on the east, Reed Market Road on the north, and Murphy Road on the south, per the Old Farm District Neighborhood Association's own boundary description. The name comes straight from the land's former use. Before Bend's growth reached this far southeast, these parcels grew food for the town. A Central Oregon Irrigation District canal still runs through the district today, a working piece of that agricultural past. The canal traces to 1902, when Alexander M. Drake, the same Drake behind downtown's Drake Park, formed the Pilot Butte Development Company and began diverting water from the Deschutes River. His company had the Central Oregon and Pilot Butte Canals built by 1907, then sold out before the irrigation district itself existed. On December 17, 1917, the company was handed over to the farmers who used it, and they organized what is now the Central Oregon Irrigation District.

That agricultural start explains a lot about the neighborhood today. Much of Old Farm District developed under Deschutes County jurisdiction, before the city annexed the area, and county code from that era asked for fewer sidewalks and did not require builders to plan streets around future traffic. The BNSF railroad and the COID canal now cut across the neighborhood with few places to cross from one side to the other. A Bend Bulletin report on the district found a concrete example of what that means. A trip that covers 1.5 miles as the crow flies can turn into a 5-mile drive once you account for where the tracks and the canal force you around. That is the honest trade-off of living here. You get more land, and historically a lower price than northwest or west Bend homes. You give up the tight street grid and short drive times those neighborhoods take for granted.

The housing stock shows three eras layered on top of each other. West of the canal, expect a mix of midcentury and early-2000s ranch-style homes and Craftsman builds, some on lots close to half an acre, holdovers from when the land was still farmland. A few of the county-era subdivisions carry a literary theme. Nottingham Square takes its street names from Robin Hood, King's Forest from the Old Testament, and The Shire from Tolkien. Because those subdivisions predate city sewer, some homes there still run on septic systems installed decades ago, and the city has been extending sewer lines through the area to phase them out. Newer subdivisions along the eastern and southern edges, including Bridges, Orion Greens, and Stone Creek, sit on city sewer and were built to current city standards from the start.

For parks, the district's anchor is Alpenglow Park, 37 acres that Bend Park and Recreation opened in 2022 at 61049 SE 15th Street. It carries a seasonal sprayground, bouldering structures, a dog off-leash area, a covered stage, and 2.2 miles of ADA-accessible paved paths. West of Silver Rail Elementary, the smaller 6.17-acre Stone Creek Park adds a bike pump track, a skills course, and a skate spot built around a basalt lava-butte feature, with a sightline toward Newberry National Volcanic Monument.

Families with school-age kids feed into Silver Rail Elementary, a K-5 school at 61530 SE Stone Creek Lane that Bend-La Pine Schools opened in September 2015 to absorb growth on this side of town. The 69,470-square-foot building runs a Gifted and Talented program and, when it opened, was the first Bend-La Pine elementary with a lunch commons separate from the gym, a layout the district reused in schools it built afterward. From there, students move to High Desert Middle School at 61000 Diamondback Lane, which enrolls roughly 693 students and offers Project Lead the Way alongside its own Gifted and Talented track.

The district is not finished changing. Just south and east of Old Farm District, Bend added 479 acres to its urban growth boundary in 2016, land the city and local press call the Elbow. In 2021 the city adopted a master plan for that land calling for roughly 1,230 new homes, an elementary school, a park, and about 2,800 jobs. As of late 2025, the city was partway through building a $26 million sewer pump station to serve it, while the arterial roads and roundabouts that growth also needs remained unfunded, an estimated $10.7 million short. For Old Farm District, that means more rooftops and more traffic arriving at the neighborhood's edge before the roads are built to carry them.

Old Farm District suits a buyer who wants more land, an older build, and a lower entry price, and who does not mind driving around a canal to reach the grocery store. It is a harder sell for someone who wants a short walk to Old Mill District or a ten-minute bike ride downtown. Buyers in Bridges, Orion Greens, or Stone Creek get current-code construction and sewer service without the county-era compromises next door, but they are still routing around the same rail line and canal as the rest of the district.

amenities.name: Alpenglow Park
amenities.description: A 37-acre community park at 61049 SE 15th Street opened in 2022, with a seasonal sprayground, bouldering structures, a dog off-leash area, 2.2 miles of ADA-accessible paved paths, and a covered stage.

amenities.name: Stone Creek Park
amenities.description: A 6.17-acre park at 61531 SE Stone Creek Lane with a bike pump track, bike skills course, skate spot, and a basalt lava-butte feature with views to Newberry National Volcanic Monument.

amenities.name: Silver Rail Elementary
amenities.description: A Bend-La Pine Schools K-5 directly east of Stone Creek Park, the primary feeder for the neighborhood.

amenities.name: High Desert Middle School
amenities.description: A Bend-La Pine Schools grades 6-8 campus at 61000 Diamondback Lane with about 693 students, offering Project Lead the Way and a Gifted and Talented program.

amenities.name: Reed Crossing Market
amenities.description: A neighborhood grocery and prepared-food market at 21185 SE Reed Market Road carrying locally sourced meat, produce, coffee, and brick-oven pizza.
amenities.access: Within the district on Reed Market Road

drive_times.note: Via Reed Market Road west or SE 15th Street north

Via SE 15th Street north and US-20 east
